subject: ACME Retail — us-west dedicated tier memory pressure and fallback coordination
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-14T09:12:00Z
Subject: PSA: us-west dedicated pool memory pressure — customer impact observed

Team,

Heads-up on an active issue affecting some customers on dedicated capacity in us-west. At ~08:55 UTC we started to see sustained memory pressure on one of the reserved GPU pools serving Tier-3 dedicated customers. Observed symptoms: elevated per-token latency (95th pctl increase), sporadic preemptions/evictions, and KV-cache thrashing for long-context requests.

Initial triage indicates a workload in that pool exhibited a steady growth in GPU-resident fragmented allocations (likely a driver-level interaction with a new model variant). The autoscaler attempted to compensate but mis-evaluated available headroom due to stale memory accounting, causing late node drain events and additional churn. Affected customers include ACME Retail (dedicated tenant id: acme-789), LuminaHealth (partial), and a small number of startups on the same party pool.

Immediate mitigations in flight (doing now):
- Redirected ACME traffic to the secondary cold-standby pool (warm-fallback) for requests under their fallback policy (manual route applied).
- Increased eviction thresholds and disabled aggressive preemption for 30 minutes to stabilize KV caches.
- Engineering is collecting GPU kernel traces and memory maps for the offending tasks.

Ask: Connor / Marissa — please lead customer comms for ACME. Karthik / Marcus — attach the kernel traces and a preliminary RCA once available. I'll prepare an ops timeline and postmortem skeleton.

I'll update in the thread as we know more.

Thanks,
Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Head of Support Escalations
Redwood Inference
From: Jenna Park <jenna.park@acme-retail.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@acme-retail.com
Date: 2028-08-14T09:45:00Z
Subject: Re: ACME Retail — us-west dedicated tier memory pressure and fallback coordination

Connor —

Thanks for the ping. We saw a burst of 5–10s tail latency on checkout APIs around 08:50–09:05 UTC which triggered our circuit breakers and degraded our experiment traffic. That window impacted ~2.1% of requests and one of our promotions misfired. The fallback to secondary pool reduced errors but not latency for longer-context inference.

We need:
- Exact timeline of what happened and confirmation that our tokens and requests were not exposed to other tenants (data isolation concern).
- A proposal for credits for the customer impact window.
- ETA for a permanent mitigation so this doesn't recur during our prime time tomorrow.

Please loop in engineering; I can be on a quick call.

—Jenna
Jenna Park
SRE, ACME Retail

Date: 2028-08-14T10:02:00Z
Subject: Re: ACME Retail — us-west dedicated tier memory pressure and fallback coordination

Jenna —

Appreciate the details and apologies for the disruption. We're standing up a quick bridge if you'd like to join; Marcus can jump into the technical details. Short answers up-front:
- We believe there was no cross-tenant data leakage — the affected work was process-level memory fragmentation, not shared KV corruption. Full verification continues.
- We're preparing a credits proposal based on your measured error/latency window; Marissa will own the formal estimate and offer.
- Fix plan: short-term patch to autoscaler memory accounting + conservative safety margins; medium-term: kernel-level fix or driver rollback if required. Expect a live mitigation deploy within 4–6 hours and an eng postmortem within 48 hours.

We can do a 10–15 minute sync at 10:20 UTC if that works for you.

Connor O'Brien
Account Lead, Strategic Customers
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-14T11:08:00Z
Subject: RE: ACME Retail — us-west dedicated tier memory pressure and fallback coordination

Connor / team —

Quick tech summary from infra: after deeper collection of traces we see the following thread:
- Root cause: a driver/allocator interaction with a newly onboarded model variant produced heavy small-object fragmentation on GPU memory; our memory accounting sampler underestimated fragmented, resident allocations during the autoscaler's evaluation window.
- Autoscaler behavior: thresholds were calibrated to aggregate free memory metrics. Fragmented allocations weren't attributed correctly, leading to late evictions (node drains started after latency rose) instead of proactive scaling.
- No evidence of data-plane leakage — each tenant's processes remained isolated. We've verified process namespaces and container image digests for ACME.

Immediate technical actions completed:
1) Forced eviction policy disabled for the affected nodes (to preserve KV cache) and warm-fallback traffic steering for ACME.
2) Hotfix queued: adjust autoscaler sampling to include fragmentation estimate and add a 12% headroom safety margin. This hotfix will be staged and deployed in two waves: canary + full deployment. Canary expected in ~3h, full in ~6h depending on canary.
3) Longer-term: patch submitted to driver team; if driver rollback is needed we'll coordinate with partner drivers — timeline ~72h for final decision.

Attachments: mem-pressure-stacktrace.txt (selected stack traces), customer-impact-summary.csv (per-tenant traffic and error windows).

I'll follow up with the canary outcome and a detailed RCA for the postmortem.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: Jenna Park <jenna.park@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-14T15:03:00Z
Subject: ACME Retail — follow-up: mitigation deployed, next steps, and customer offer

Jenna —

Thanks again for the quick sync earlier. Short update:
- Canary of autoscaler sampling hotfix completed at 13:30 UTC with no regression; full rollout completed at 14:50 UTC. Observed metrics: 95th pctl latency for your workload returned to baseline within ~12 minutes after full rollout.
- We validated tenant isolation via container digests and process namespace checks — no cross-tenant reads or KV corruption.

What we are delivering to ACME now:
1) Credit offer: 5% usage credit for the 08:50–09:10 UTC impact window (Marissa will follow up with a concrete credit amount and HubSpot deal update).
2) Postmortem: eng will deliver a formatted RCA and timeline within 48 hours. Early draft will be available in the linked Drive folder.
3) Runbook changes: autoscaler now includes fragmentation-aware sampling and a 12% headroom; we will add an alert rule specific to fragmentation spikes and an automated traffic steer to warm-fallback pools to remove manual steps.

Attachments (for your reference): uswest_incident_timeline.pdf — timeline with events and operator notes.

If you'd like a post-incident review call with eng + product, we can schedule one — propose Tuesday 08:00–09:00 PT.

Connor O'Brien
Account Lead, Strategic Customers
Redwood Inference
